newsitem.title: FRANCE: BIS sees 1996 loss after charges.
newsitem.headline: BIS sees 1996 loss after charges.

text.p: French temporary work agency BIS said that it expected a 1996 net loss of between 80 and 120 million francs after charges.

The company, in which Dutch Vendex recently acquired a 60 percent stake, said it had to make a 215 million charge on the sale of loans of Caisse Fonciere de Credit and another 65 million on the sale of its security division.
"Without these non-recurring items the net profit would have been between 120 to 160 million francs," it said.
BIS said the 1996 operating profit would be less than 350 million francs against more than 500 million in 1995.
BIS said that it did not expect its profit margins to improve in 1997 but did see an increase in sales.
It said its net debt at December 31, 1996, would be some 130 million francs against 137 million in the previous year.
